root_idea.summary: Forceful contact between two things, as though one strikes the other.
root_idea.development: This central image develops into striking, reciprocal collision, forceful closure, and descriptions of bodily collision or strength.

senses.definition: To slap the face with the open hand.
senses.usage_conditions: In the supplied Quran occurrence, the verb is a feminine singular perfect form with the face as its object; the construction specifically describes an open-handed slap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike a person or thing forcefully, with the hand, an object, or anything capable of striking; of a hawk or falcon, to strike prey with the foot and knock it down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression أَوَّلَ صَكٍّ denotes a first blow or first striking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To push or thrust someone or something.
To shut or close a door, or to lock it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with a door as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To write a صَكّ, a formal written instrument or document.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the verb associated with producing the document called صَكٌّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be knock-kneed, with the knees colliding; of an animal, to have hocks that collide in movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to humans and also to animals such as horses and ostriches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike someone or something, including forcefully or with the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form III usage; the object may be a person or thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For two people or bodies to strike one another; for knees to collide or swords to clash.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal construction, including the expression for two knees knocking together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A written instrument: a debenture or written acknowledgment of a debt, property, transaction, contract, judicial decision, or an order for payment of an allowance or stipend.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural forms include أَصُكٌّ, صِكَاكٌ, and صُكُوكٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The most intense midday heat of summer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially in the conventional expression صَكَّةَ عُمَىٍّ, describing meeting someone in the blinding heat of summer midday.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The air or atmosphere between heaven and earth.
Weak, especially one regarded as weak because he is struck frequently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage in which the form has the sense of a passive participle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A writer of صِكَاك documents, including an actuary who records a judge’s sentences.
Knock-kneed, with the knees or hocks colliding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a person or to an animal such as a horse or ostrich.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Strong or robust; specifically, a head strong enough to butt or knock against other heads.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to people and animals, including camels and asses; the head-specific sense occurs in رَأْسٌ مِصَكٌّ لِلرُّؤُوسِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Fleshy, as an epithet of a camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The explanation pictures flesh as having been thrust into the camel; the usage is reported specifically of camels.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The Quranic slap and the broader forceful-striking branch are represented.
Identifies the verbal noun of صَكَّ without adding lexical meaning.
Conventional term for intense summer midday heat.
Weak person, especially one frequently struck.
The same adjective applied to teeth that cleave closely is included in the target’s collocational branch.
Head strong for butting is a collocational specialization of the attested strength sense.
